name: Coarse-Geometric KW Bounds (CG-KW)

primitives.name: KW_metric_space
primitives.description: For boolean f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1}, the set X_f = f^{-1}(0) x f^{-1}(1) equipped with the disagreement-Hamming metric d((x,y),(x',y')) = |{i : (x_i!=y_i) XOR (x'_i!=y'_i)}|. Implementable as a sparse weighted graph; distances computed by BFS.

primitives.name: AsymDim_cover
primitives.description: A family {U_a}_{a in A} of subsets of X_f with uniformly bounded diameter and bounded r-multiplicity (every r-ball meets <= k+1 sets). Encoded as a hypergraph; checking the bound is a polynomial-time predicate in |X_f|.

primitives.name: Hilbert_compression_embedding
primitives.description: A map phi: X_f -> R^N with explicit upper Lipschitz constant L and lower compression rho(t) ~ t^alpha, certified by a Gram matrix and PSD check. Computable via SDP.

primitives.name: Coarse_partition_tree
primitives.description: A binary tree whose leaves partition X_f into 'monochromatic' coordinate-rectangles; each internal node is labeled with a coordinate i in [n] separating left/right by x_i vs y_i disagreement. This is exactly the syntactic object dual to a KW-protocol.

primitives.name: Property_A_witness
primitives.description: Maps xi: X_f -> ell^1(X_f) of finite support such that ||xi_x - xi_y||_1 is small when d(x,y) bounded, and supports lie in fixed-radius balls. Verifiable by linear programming.

operations.name: coarsen
operations.description: Quotient by r-balls; produces a coarser space whose asymptotic dimension is preserved.

operations.name: tree_to_cover
operations.description: Each leaf of a depth-d KW tree gives a covering set; multiplicity is bounded by tree depth.

operations.name: compose
operations.signature: (KW_metric_space f, KW_metric_space g) -> KW_metric_space (f o g)
operations.description: Coarse fiber product modeling block-composition; coarse invariants must satisfy super-additivity here (the KRW analogue).

operations.name: embed_into_Hilbert
operations.description: Compute (via SDP relaxation) the optimal Hilbert compression exponent alpha*(X_f).

operations.name: asym_dim
operations.description: Compute (or lower bound via LP duality) the asymptotic dimension asdim(X_f).

operations.name: pad
operations.description: Direct product with a k-cube; used to amplify coarse invariants.

target_invariant.name: formula_depth_D(f)
target_invariant.what_it_should_bound: log_2 of minimum size, equivalently minimum depth, of a De Morgan formula computing f. The framework conjectures D(f) >= c * asdim(X_f) and D(f) >= c' / alpha*(X_f), giving super-logarithmic depth lower bounds when X_f has no Hilbert compression (Yu 2000; Nowak-Yu 2012).

axioms_tentative: A1 (Tree-to-Dimension): Every depth-d KW protocol yields an AsymDim_cover of X_f with multiplicity <= d+1 and bounded diameter; hence asdim(X_f) <= D(f).

A2 (Compression Lower Bound): If X_f admits a Hilbert embedding with compression exponent alpha, then D(f) >= Omega(1/alpha); contrapositively, expander-like X_f forces large depth (cf. Gromov's a-T-menability obstructions).
A3 (Coarse Composition / KRW): asdim(X_{f o g}) >= asdim(X_f) + asdim(X_g) - O(1), giving a coarse-geometric route to the Karchmer-Raz-Wigderson conjecture.

A4 (Non-Naturalness): The predicate 'asdim(X_f) >= k' is neither large nor constructive in the Razborov-Rudich sense - random functions have bounded asdim with high probability because random metric spaces of bounded degree have asdim 0 in the coarse sense, so this invariant evades the natural proof

A5 (Non-Relativizing / Non-Algebrizing): Coarse invariants depend on the fine combinatorial structure of f^{-1}(0) and f^{-1}(1) as embedded in the Hamming cube, not on oracle access or low-degree algebraic extensions, so oracle and algebraic-extension transformations do not preserve asdim or alpha*
